intended_object: The real period Ω(W) = ∫_{E(ℝ)} |ω| of a real Weierstrass curve, ω = dx/(2y+a₁x+a₃) the invariant differential, as in the BSD formula (Silverman III.1, App. C). Inferred from the docstring and module documentation.
explanation: On the curve, (2y+a₁x+a₃)² = Ψ₂Sq(x). Over each x with Ψ₂Sq(x) > 0 there are two real points, and |ω| = dx/√Ψ₂Sq(x) on each. The roots of Ψ₂Sq and the point at infinity have measure zero. So ∫_{E(ℝ)}|ω| = 2∫_{Ψ₂Sq>0} dx/√Ψ₂Sq(x), which is exactly `2 * realPeriodLIntegral.toReal`. Let ω₁ be the least positive real period of the lattice. This gives ω₁ when Δ<0 and 2ω₁ when Δ>0 (both real components counted). That matches the BSD Ω = c_∞·ω₁ that the docstring describes ("∫|ω| over the real points"). If the integral diverges (possible for singular curves), the value is 0; this junk value is documented, and the library proves finiteness for elliptic curves. The notion is inherently over ℝ, so the setting is natural. Mathlib has no definition of a period of an elliptic curve.
